claims.location: source name and comment[data file] rows 1-17
claims.value: 15 named Pongo fossil enamel specimens and two extraction blanks mapped to 17 Thermo RAW files
claims.evidence: PRIDE lists exactly 17 associated RAW entries. The deposited README names 15 fossil specimen IDs and identifies two blank controls. Seven README rows for run IDs 1899, 1901, 1902, 1904, 1905, 1906 and 1907 have the wrong 20210415_EXPL8 prefix; the public RAW files have 20210422_EXPL2. The trailing acquisition numbers are unique and match exactly, so the specimen map uses those numbers while data-file values use the actual public filenames.

claims.location: characteristics[organism], characteristics[organism part], characteristics[disease], characteristics[developmental stage], characteristics[strain or breed], characteristics[sex]
claims.value: Pongo sp. fossil tooth enamel; unknown disease, developmental stage, strain and sex; blank rows not applicable
claims.evidence: PRIDE identifies Pongo sp.; protocol and paper specify ancient enamel flakes from fossil orangutan teeth. No per-specimen sex or disease assignment is in the deposited file map. Extraction blanks have no organism or organism part.

claims.value: one run per distinct specimen or blank source
claims.evidence: The README assigns a distinct specimen ID to each enamel RAW and a distinct acquisition to each blank; no repeated source or technical reinjection is identified.

claims.location: comment[instrument], comment[proteomics data acquisition method], comment[dissociation method]
claims.evidence: PRIDE protocol and linked paper LC-MS/MS section specify Exploris 480, data-dependent top-10 acquisition and HCD product ions.
PRIDE sample processing protocol and paper Protein extraction section explicitly describe a digestion-free enamel peptide recovery protocol.

claims.location: comment[precursor mass tolerance], comment[fragment mass tolerance]
claims.value: 4.5 ppm final-search precursor and 20 ppm fragment
claims.evidence: PRIDE data processing protocol gives default first and final search tolerances of 20 and 4.5 ppm respectively, plus 20 ppm fragment tolerance.

limitations: The README acquisition prefix is wrong for seven entries; specimen assignments are linked by unique trailing run number, while exact public RAW names are retained in the SDRF.
The study compares fossil diversity without a single controlled experimental factor; specimen IDs are source names, not factor values.
The automated PRIDE reconciler flags not applicable cleavage because it expects a named enzyme, but the accession-specific protocol explicitly says digestion-free.
Fossil specimens are not assigned to living Pongo species from morphometric affinities; organism remains Pongo sp. as in PRIDE.
